stories.label: North Korea plants 960,000 mines in DMZ since 2024
stories.summary: South Korea's Joint Chiefs say North Korea has laid nearly a million landmines along the DMZ since 2024, turning a ceasefire line into a fortified border, while Seoul answers by proposing military talks. Lead with the 960,000 figure and what it means: Pyongyang is sealing itself off under its 'two hostile states' doctrine, not preparing to cross. Context from the NYT: the North's missiles and drones are now battle-tested in Russia's war.

stories.label: Israel's Ben-Gvir calls for dismantling the Palestinian Authority
stories.summary: After a shooting at a Hebron checkpoint wounded Israeli soldiers, Netanyahu ordered Hebron locked down and Ben-Gvir demanded the Palestinian Authority be dismantled, days before Israel's elections. Lead with the collective punishment: a city of some 200,000 Palestinians sealed over one attack, and a minister using it to campaign for ending the only Palestinian governing body in the West Bank. Attribute the attack details to Israel's account; this follows Guterres calling settler violence out of control.

stories.label: WHO warns 'more complex' Ebola outbreak now present in 3 African countries
stories.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak that began in DR Congo has killed more than 4,600 people and reached Nigeria, and the head of Africa CDC now says authorities underestimated it. Lead with the death toll and the jump to Africa's most populous country; the accountability question is who misjudged the spread and why there is no licensed vaccine for this strain. Who bears it: health workers and border communities in Congo, Uganda and Nigeria.

stories.label: ECB Says Consumers' Inflation Expectations Edge Up in September
stories.summary: Euro-area households now expect 3.1% inflation over the next year, up from 3%, the ECB's survey shows, ahead of next week's rate decision. Lead with why: the Iran war's energy shock is feeding into what households expect to pay, which locks in the ECB's hiking path. Name the series: the ECB rate and the euro. Reuters frames the meeting's five questions, including France.

stories.label: Gold heads for steep weekly loss as oil prices fuel Fed rate concerns
stories.summary: Gold is heading for its steepest weekly fall in over four months, near $4,021 an ounce, because the Gulf war's oil prices push the Fed toward keeping rates higher for longer. Lead with the counterintuitive chain: a war that should lift a haven instead sinks it via oil, inflation and the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding metal. Name the series: gold, Brent crude and the Fed rate, ahead of next week's Fed meeting.

stories.label: Insulin product in short supply after German manufacturer halts supplies, NA told
stories.summary: Pakistan's type 1 diabetics face a shortage of an insulin product after its German manufacturer halted supplies while upgrading its line, the health ministry told the National Assembly. Lead with who pays: children and adults who cannot skip a dose, in a country that depends on one foreign supplier. The mechanism is a single-source import dependency for an essential medicine, and the question is what the regulator is doing about substitutes and prices.

stories.label: OpenAI估值目标缩水万亿！IPO前再募资2016亿元
stories.summary: OpenAI is seeking up to $30 billion before its IPO at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, $150 billion below September's target, with Coatue and an Emirati investor leading and a UAE compute deal under discussion. Lead with the cut valuation alongside the Gulf money: the UAE is buying a seat in frontier AI with capital and data centres. Context: Anthropic is reported to be targeting $1.5-2 trillion; AI jitters already moved the yen this week.

stories.label: Why is SK hynix ADR stock surging today? By Investing.com
stories.summary: SK hynix has suspended a pre-IPO round and a possible Nasdaq listing for Solidigm, its US NAND flash subsidiary, and its shares jumped 5%. Lead with the decision, not the price: the world's AI memory leader is keeping its US storage arm in-house as AI data centres drive flash demand. Explain what Solidigm is (Intel's former NAND business) and why investors rewarded keeping it.

stories.label: Malaysian PM Anwar Bans Civil Servants From Using Israel-developed Navigation App
stories.summary: Anwar Ibrahim has barred Malaysian civil servants from using Waze, built in Tel Aviv before Google bought it in 2013, saying it could be exploited by the Israeli state. Lead with the mechanism: location data from a government workforce as a security exposure, and how far app origin matters once a US giant owns it. Compare with other states' bans on foreign apps for officials.

stories.label: Just 3% of the world's glaciers account for over half of glacier ice loss
stories.summary: Glaciers that end in lakes, the ocean or ice shelves are 3.2% of the world's glaciers but lost 134 billion tonnes of ice a year from 2000 to 2019, over half of all glacier loss, a new study finds. Lead with the 3%-to-half ratio and the mechanism: water at the glacier front melts and calves ice far faster than air. Name where these glaciers are and what it means for sea-level and water-supply forecasts.

stories.label: Gulf on cusp of new war as Trump hints at 'imminent' Iran action
stories.summary: New development since the 10-21 coverage (when the White House said no strike before the 3 November midterms): The Atlantic reports Trump is weighing several days of strikes right after the midterms on nuclear sites, missiles and energy infrastructure, and Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei answers that Tehran could hit US-linked oil facilities, data centres and AI sites across the Gulf, warning of three years of energy turmoil. Lead with the target lists on both sides: Gulf states that host US assets carry the cost. Brent crude near $100 is the market stake.

stories.label: UAE Paid Swiss Intelligence Firm to Compile Database of “Hostile” Facebook Users
stories.summary: Leaked documents show the UAE paid Swiss firm Alp Services to build lists of UAE residents based on which news articles critical of the Emirati government they had liked on Facebook. The mechanism to lead with: a single 'like' becomes a dossier entry, and a European private intelligence firm does the profiling a state could not easily do in the open. Name who commissioned the work, who was listed and what the documents say was done with the lists.

stories.label: Trump says Musk restored Ukraine's Starlink access amid Russia war
stories.summary: Follows the 10-20 story on Starlink cutting out above 130 km/h for Ukrainian drones. New: Trump says Musk has restored Ukraine's access (The Hindu reports the claim covers Starshield, the military variant), but Zelensky and Ukrainian military sources say speeds have not changed. Lead with the gap between the claim and the front line: one private company's settings decide whether a country's drones work, and the only check on it is the word of two men.

stories.label: Venezuelans demand elections in first national protest in nearly two years
stories.summary: A new development after the 10-22 story on blackout protests in Maracaibo: thousands marched in several cities in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, demanding free elections. No date has been set to choose a successor since US forces captured Maduro, and Delcy Rodríguez still governs. Lead with the gap: the man is gone but the vote has not come, and ask who decides when it does, Caracas or Washington.

stories.label: China's Antarctic marine protected area has a Soviet name, with more Russian fingerprints emerging
stories.summary: A Daily Maverick investigation: after a decade of blocking Southern Ocean marine reserves alongside Moscow at CCAMLR, Beijing has proposed its own, in the Soviet-named Cosmonauts Sea, and its bid to rewrite the commission's conservation rules mirrors changes Russia has pushed. Lead with the mechanism: CCAMLR works by consensus, so two states can block everyone else's reserves and then write the rules for their own. The stake is krill fishing and who controls the Antarctic commons.

stories.label: Chinese Copper Smelters Plan More Output Cuts Ahead of Fee Talks
stories.summary: Chinese smelters, which process most of the world's copper ore, plan more output cuts ahead of the annual talks with miners on treatment fees, because ore is so scarce that processing fees have collapsed. Meanwhile Grupo México is spending to restart Asarco's Hayden smelter in Arizona after its copper output fell. Lead with who holds the leverage now, miners or smelters, and the US effort to rebuild refining at home. Name copper prices.

stories.label: Some of Europe's highest energy costs expected in Britain this winter
stories.summary: The energy system operators' official winter outlook says Great Britain will keep the lights on only by paying some of Europe's highest prices for imported gas and power, as its import dependence deepens. Britain still imports almost 60% of its gas, and it is buying LNG against Asia while the Gulf war threatens supply. This is the operators' forecast, not the 10-21 Carbon Brief point on how gas sets bills. Lead with what it costs to be a price-taker. Name natural gas prices.

stories.label: Hacking attempts surge as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
stories.summary: A new development since the 10-21 story on governments taking sites offline: cloud firms now report a surge of exploitation attempts against the PHP flaws (PHP2Shell, 154k Wikipedia views yesterday) as companies and governments from Tokyo to Beijing to Amsterdam rush to patch. Lead with the race between disclosure and exploitation, and give numbers from the cloud firms. The reader runs PHP servers, and much of the web's long tail will never be patched.

stories.label: 1元甩卖内地业务，快狗打车为何输掉同城货运生意？
stories.summary: Kuaigou Dache (GOGOX), once a listed rival to Huolala, is selling its mainland China business for one yuan after losing the subsidy war in same-city freight. Lead with the one-yuan price, then the mechanism: in China's platform economy, logistics apps compete on subsidies paid by whoever has the deepest pockets, and the drivers' margins pay for the loser's exit. This is the mainland tech press's own account.

stories.label: Four KJ-3000 Radar Jets At Chinese Factory Point To Serial Production
stories.summary: Satellite imagery of the Shaanxi factory shows four KJ-3000 airborne early-warning jets, the most capable in China's AEW&C fleet, which means the type is now in serial production. Lead with the count from open-source imagery and what it means: AEW&C aircraft are what let a fighter force see and fight beyond its own coast, as the USAF itself rethinks how it fights air-to-air.

stories.label: Casualties reported after 7.0 quake strikes China's Tibet
stories.summary: A magnitude-7.0 quake at 18km depth hit Nagqu in Tibet late Thursday; News18 reports 16 dead and 32 injured, houses collapsed and power and telecoms cut (GDACS Red alert). Lead with the toll and say it is early and comes via Xinhua citing local officials. Mechanism: a remote, high-altitude region where rescue depends on a few roads and where Beijing controls access and information; note the January 2025 Dingri quake as precedent. Filed as politics, a disaster, not science.

stories.label: Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye to meet European trio in Istanbul
stories.summary: Turkey hosts the R-4 (Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkey) and then an R-4 plus E-3 (Britain, France, Germany) foreign ministers' meeting in Istanbul on 23 October. Lead with who is at the table: four Muslim-majority powers formed this bloc in March to mediate the Gulf war and are now bringing Europe in, without Washington. Tie it to Munir's proposals to Tehran and Macron's Riyadh trip this week, and say what the bloc can and cannot deliver.

stories.label: Deputado detido após atingir jornalista com um tiro defendeu liberação de armas em 2017
stories.summary: A Brazilian state deputy, Marcelo Aguiar, was detained after shooting a journalist days before Brazil's tied presidential runoff, and Agência Pública found that in 2017, in Congress, he filed a bill to repeal the Disarmament Statute. Lead with the shooting and the bill. Mechanism: Bolsonaro-era gun liberalisation put more firearms in political hands, and violence against the press and students (the UFRN beating this week) is rising in the campaign's last days.

stories.label: Venezuela faces a deepening energy crisis as protests grow
stories.summary: Prolonged blackouts across Venezuela are pushing residents into street protests. Lead with who loses power and for how long. Mechanism: a country with the world's largest proven oil reserves cannot keep its lights on because the Guri hydro system and thermal plants have decayed under mismanagement and sanctions, and the government answers with rationing schedules instead of investment.

stories.label: Inflation and borrowing data illustrate chancellor's Budget challenge
stories.summary: Write Bloomberg's Mexico story, the primary link: annual inflation sped up to 3.62% in the first half of October, above forecasts, which pressures Banxico to rethink a five-month hold on interest rates at next month's meeting. The BBC source in this cluster is about UK inflation and borrowing ahead of the Budget; use it only as a brief parallel. Lead with the 3.62% figure and who pays when food and fuel prices rise, and name Banxico's policy rate as the series to watch.

stories.label: China's Bank Wealth Management Market Reaches 35.4 Trillion Yuan
stories.summary: Chinese savers held 35.4 trillion yuan ($5.3 trillion) in bank wealth-management products at the end of September, up 10.1% in a year, as they moved money out of property and stocks into safer products. Lead with the figure and what it shows: households are not spending, which is the deflation problem Beijing is trying to solve. Name the yuan as the series.

stories.label: Comcast loses more customers, claims other ISPs' cheap prices are "irrational"
stories.summary: Comcast lost 144,000 residential broadband customers in Q3, up from 91,000 a year earlier, as fiber and fixed-wireless rivals undercut it. It calls their prices 'irrational' and plans cable job cuts and more AI agents. Lead with the customer loss and the 'irrational' line: a near-monopoly incumbent is losing to competition and answers by replacing workers with AI. Dateline Philadelphia.

stories.label: Malaysia precious metal recycling plant to supply gold for chipmaking
stories.summary: Japan's Tanaka Precious Metal Group is forming a joint venture in Malaysia to recover gold and other precious metals from semiconductor and electronics manufacturing scrap. Lead with why: with gold near record prices, recycling chip-plant waste is cheaper than buying new metal, and Malaysia's packaging and testing industry makes the scrap. Name gold prices as the series.

stories.label: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business
stories.summary: New development on our story about eMudhra's compromised private keys: the Indian certificate authority now says it will leave the global SSL/TLS certificate business. Lead with the exit decision. Mechanism: browsers distrust a CA after a key compromise, which ends its business. Say what happens to the sites holding its certificates and to India's push for a home-grown root of trust. The HN thread (860 points) is public attention, not a source. Dateline Bengaluru.

stories.label: Portal Texas Used to ‘Rubber Stamp’ Data Centers Down After 404 Media Reporting
stories.summary: Texas's environmental regulator (TCEQ) took down the online permit portal that 404 Media showed was auto-approving data-centre applications, and commissioners now promise staff will review every application to see whether it is for a data centre. Lead with the accountability result: reporting forced a regulator to stop rubber-stamping the AI build-out's air and water permits. Dateline Austin.

stories.label: Toronto crime tips org freezes operations after details of data breach come to light
stories.summary: Toronto Crime Stoppers paused operations and broke with the national association, publishing a timeline of what it knew about a data breach and when. Lead with the stakes: an anonymous tip line exists to protect informants, and a breach can expose people who reported violent crime. Name who held the data and who delayed disclosure. Dateline Toronto.

stories.label: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.
stories.summary: NASA's latest estimate is that one Artemis crewed Moon landing needs 22 Starship launches, most of them tankers to refuel the lander in orbit, a number the agency has guarded closely. Lead with 22. Mechanism: cryogenic propellant transfer in orbit has never been shown at scale, so the whole landing schedule depends on a launch cadence nobody has achieved, while China's crewed lunar program runs on a simpler architecture.

stories.label: International Criminal Court Wins E.U.'s Top Human Rights Prize
stories.summary: The European Parliament gave the Sakharov Prize to the ICC itself, an institution, while Washington has sanctioned its judges and prosecutor for the Netanyahu and Gallant warrants. Lead with the collision: Europe's legislature honours the court the US is trying to cripple. Explain what the US sanctions do in practice (frozen assets, banking cut-offs for judges) and whether the EU has done anything binding, such as activating its blocking statute, beyond giving a prize.

stories.label: UN chief to travel to Egypt Friday
stories.summary: Guterres said settler violence in the occupied West Bank is 'simply out of control' and aimed at driving Palestinian communities off their land, and he flies to Egypt on Friday. Lead with the named actors: armed settlers, operating under Israeli military protection, emptying villages. Give the latest UN OCHA counts of attacks and of displaced communities, and explain what the Cairo trip is for (Gaza crossings, aid). The story is the dispossession, not the travel schedule.

stories.label: Carney and Erdogan launch 'strong and resilient' Canada-Turkiye partnership
stories.summary: Canada and Türkiye signed a strategic partnership in Ankara with agreements on the defence industry, air transport and energy. Al-Monitor frames it as part of Carney's push to cut Canada's reliance on the US. Lead with the reversal: Ottawa embargoed drone optics exports to Türkiye in 2020–21 over Nagorno-Karabakh, and now signs a defence-industry pact. A middle power is hedging away from Washington by going to another middle power.

stories.label: Exclusive: UN abandons Rafah crossing; PHP flaws expose websites; AIPAC ends endorsements
stories.summary: Write only the lead item, Drop Site's exclusive that the UN is pulling out of the Rafah crossing, and ignore the PHP and AIPAC items in the same newsletter. Lead with what the withdrawal means for Gazans who need medical evacuation and aid. Name who now controls the crossing and on what terms, and say why the UN left (Israeli restrictions, staff safety). Attribute it as Drop Site reporting; this follows our 10-22 story on the cancer patient arrested at Rafah.

stories.label: Italy and Spain lift border controls after months of tension over Ceuta
stories.summary: More than 70,000 people crossed irregularly from Morocco into Ceuta in late July, and Italy answered by reimposing checks on Spanish citizens, breaking Schengen between two founding members for three months. Lead with the scale of the crossing and the precedent: one country's migration surge suspended free movement inside the bloc. Then ask what happened to the 70,000, and what Rabat's role at the fence was before and after.

stories.label: ‘Citizens’ health’ session at Egypt Forum 2026 boasts spending success with no mention of declining hospital bed numbers
stories.summary: At Egypt Forum 2026, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar praised 'unprecedented' state support for health care, while Egypt's own statistics show hospital beds per person falling. Lead with that gap between the claim and the count. Give the bed numbers Mada Masr cites, and the share of health spending that patients pay out of pocket, which is the cost the forum left out.

stories.label: "Unethical" vaccine trial on babies backed by RFK Jr. is formally canceled
stories.summary: Guinea-Bissau formally rejected a US-funded trial, run by Danish researchers, that would have withheld the birth dose of hepatitis B vaccine from newborns to look for 'nonspecific harms', after police had already seized the doses. Lead with the ethics: the trial would have denied a proven vaccine to African babies in a country with high hepatitis B prevalence, to test a claim promoted by RFK Jr. Explain mother-to-child transmission and why the birth dose is the standard. Dateline Bissau.

stories.label: National Academies Rank Nonpolar Moon Sites
stories.summary: Every Artemis landing is planned for the lunar south pole, chasing water ice. A National Academies report now ranks the four best non-polar sites for crewed missions. Lead with the scientific case: which questions about the Moon's volcanic history, its age and the early solar system can only be answered away from the pole. Name the four sites and what each could tell us.

stories.label: Qatar locks in US LNG through 2054 as it looks beyond Hormuz
stories.summary: QatarEnergy, owner of the world's largest single gas field, has agreed to buy up to 4 million tonnes a year of US LNG through 2054. It is buying gas it cannot ship out of the Gulf, because IRGC mines and tanker strikes threaten ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Lead with the inversion: an exporter becomes a buyer to keep its customer contracts. Name the series: natural gas prices and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: China bets on manufactured water, and wants to sell it to the world
stories.summary: Shrinking water supplies at home pushed Beijing into desalination and filtration, and Chinese firms now sell membranes and whole plants to dry countries across Asia, the Middle East and Africa. Lead with the dependency this creates: Gulf and North African states whose drinking water runs on Chinese membranes. Give market-share figures where the source has them, and compare it with what China did in solar panels.

stories.label: Mexico’s year of oil spills fuels growing concern
stories.summary: Pemex, Mexico's state oil company and the world's most indebted oil major, has spilled oil repeatedly this year, and fishing communities say they are not compensated and regulators do not hold it to account. Lead with the number of spills and who pays for them: fishers on the Gulf coast. The mechanism: a state company that the state cannot afford to police. Dateline at the worst spill site.

stories.label: High court sets aside multi-billion ARV tender awards over procurement irregularities
stories.summary: South Africa runs the world's largest HIV treatment programme, and a high court has found parts of the health department's multibillion-rand antiretroviral tender unlawful. The department must redo the awards within 120 days, while current suppliers keep delivering so that patients are not left short. Lead with the stakes: roughly 6 million people on ARVs depend on this contract. Name the irregularities, the losing bidders and Cipla, and the possible bid-rigging investigation. Dateline Pretoria.

stories.label: EU-Länder einig beim Daten-Omnibus: Mehr KI-Training, weniger Datenschutz
stories.summary: EU member states agreed their Council position on the 'data omnibus' on Wednesday. It frees personal data for AI training, widens trade-secret protection and weakens GDPR rights. Lead with the precedent: the bloc that set the global privacy standard is relaxing it for AI companies. Name which GDPR provisions change (legitimate interest for training, access-request limits) and say that trilogue talks with Parliament come next. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: Microsoft blames ConnectWise attacks on Chinese state hacker using ARTEX AI agents
stories.summary: Microsoft attributes the ConnectWise supply-chain attack to a Chinese state-aligned group running automated AI agents ('ARTEX'), and says the same tooling is now probing organisations worldwide. Lead with the mechanism: one remote-management vendor gives access to thousands of downstream networks, and AI agents make exploiting that access cheap and fast. Name the group and the sectors targeted, and give Beijing's denial if there is one.

stories.label: AI Is Already 'Amplifying the Destruction' of War
stories.summary: The international humanitarian law experts who write the Laws of Armed Conflict want guardrails on AI targeting and weapons systems. Lead with the concrete harm already documented: AI target-generation in Gaza producing strikes faster than humans can verify them. Name who is drafting the rules (ICRC, the experts 404 Media spoke to) and which states are resisting binding limits.

stories.label: Long-End US Yield Hits One-Month Low as AI Fears Fuel Haven Bid
stories.summary: Tesla's and Meta's outlooks revived doubts that AI spending will pay, Asian equities fell, and money ran to Treasuries: long-end yields hit a one-month low even with oil above $110, which would normally push them up. Lead with that tension — a war-driven oil shock and an AI-driven flight to safety pulling the US 10-year Treasury yield in opposite directions — and say what lower yields mean for borrowers such as Pakistan (Dawn). Name the US 10-year Treasury yield. Dateline New York.

stories.label: China urges opening Bab al-Mandeb in first joint statement with regional nation
stories.summary: Beijing has for the first time put its name to a formal statement on Red Sea shipping, in a communique with Djibouti, the small state that hosts China's only overseas naval base alongside US, French and Japanese ones. Lead with the shift: China depends on the strait for its Europe trade yet has left its security to others; experts say Chinese naval escorts are still unlikely, so the question is what the words commit it to. Name ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb and set it against the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia this week.

stories.label: Oil prices jump after US orders diplomats to leave Middle East
stories.summary: Brent crude futures rose to about $110 on the US order for diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia, yet Bloomberg reports the price of physical barrels is sliding at the same moment. Lead with that split: paper traders are pricing fear of Houthi strikes on Saudi oil, while refiners buying real cargoes see enough supply. The Brent price and the Houthi attacks were covered this week; the new development is the divergence between futures and physical oil, and what it says about who is betting and who is buying.

stories.label: Meta's new nonvoting shares create an overhang -- and Wall Street wants it gone
stories.summary: When Zuckerberg told Meta's board he might sell his home and leave California, the board rewrote the share structure: a new nonvoting Class C stock that lets Meta raise money for its AI spending without diluting his control. Lead with the mechanism: shareholders fund the company while one man keeps the vote, and investors now see the new shares as an overhang on the price. Meta's New Mexico verdict and Muse were covered this week; this is the governance decision.

stories.label: Delhi's Winter Season of Polluted Air Begins
stories.summary: Delhi's air index sat around 253 for a second day, three stations already in the 'very poor' band, and the first stage of the emergency curbs (GRAP-1) is in force across the capital region. Lead with the predictability: the same crop-burning, traffic and winter inversion return every October, and the response is still a graded list of temporary bans rather than a fix. Who breathes it is the story: outdoor workers and children in the worst-hit districts.

stories.label: What Is Shamonda Virus? How Does It Spread From Animals To Humans?
stories.summary: French health authorities have confirmed the first human infection ever recorded with Shamonda virus, a midge-borne virus known from cattle, in a severely immunocompromised patient near Lyon who died in early October. Lead with the jump to a new host; then the mechanism (biting midges, a virus family related to Schmallenberg) and why authorities and the ECDC call the public risk low. Datelined Lyon.

stories.label: Israeli forces arrest cancer patient, daughter returning to Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli forces arrested a Palestinian cancer patient and her daughter on Tuesday evening as they returned to Gaza through the reopened Rafah crossing after treatment in Egypt, according to their family speaking to Mada Masr. Lead with the two women by what they were doing: coming home from chemotherapy. The mechanism: Israel controls who passes through a crossing on Egypt's border, so medical evacuation becomes a checkpoint, and a patient who leaves Gaza for care risks detention on the way back.

stories.label: Ogun schools shut again as toxic gas sends over 100 pupils to hospital
stories.summary: More than 100 pupils in Ogun State were hospitalised after another exposure to an unidentified toxic gas, and schools closed again, bringing the count since April to over 300 children and teachers. Lead with the six months without an answer: the accountability gap is that the state has still not named the source, while families keep sending children back. Ask who regulates the industrial sites around Ijebu.

stories.label: Deadly gold rush continues as latest landslide kills four in Sumatra
stories.summary: Four miners died in a landslide at an illegal gold pit in South Solok, West Sumatra, the latest in a string of deaths as record gold prices pull more people into unlicensed mining. Lead with the link between the gold price and the death toll: a war-driven rally on world markets is paid for in collapsed pits and mercury-poisoned rivers in Indonesia. Name gold as the series.

stories.label: All tropical coral reefs could collapse within 50 years | New Scientist
stories.summary: The IUCN told the UN biodiversity conference that shallow-water tropical coral reefs are at high risk of disappearing by 2075, an assessment of the whole ecosystem rather than single species. Lead with the date; then who loses: the coastal fishing communities of Indonesia, the Philippines, East Africa and the Pacific that live off reef fisheries and rely on reefs to break storm waves.

stories.label: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
stories.summary: For three days this month unknown attackers controlled 333 Tor exit nodes, reconfigured to favour unencrypted email and to route SSH connections through their own servers. Lead with the number and what it means: Tor hides who you are, not what you send, and the people who rely on it most (dissidents and journalists) are exposed whenever traffic leaves the network unencrypted.

stories.label: Can LLMs Supercharge Geolocations? Our Tests Show Big Improvements But Humans Remain Key
stories.summary: Bellingcat ran its own tests after Anthropic claimed its models approach 'superhuman' photo geolocation. Lead with what the tests found, where models now succeed and where they still fail, and why it matters both ways: the tool that helps investigators verify war-crime footage also lets anyone locate a person from a single photo.

stories.label: 全国产芯片训练的大模型来了！百万上下文，价格比DeepSeek V4.1 Flash更低
stories.summary: iFlytek released Spark X2.6, a model trained entirely on Chinese-made chips, with a million-token context and API prices below DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash. Lead with the domestic-chip training: iFlytek says training on its 10,000-card Feixing-2 cluster went from 4.5 months to 1.2 and cache hit rates rose from 63% to 95.7%. That is the answer US export controls were meant to prevent. Use the Chinese tech-press view, not only the Western one.

stories.label: Geheimdienstreform: Opposition kritisiert ungeregelte Überwachung mit Werbedaten
stories.summary: The Bundestag is debating new powers for the BND and the Verfassungsschutz, but the bill says nothing on whether the agencies may buy location and ad-tracking data the advertising industry collected illegally. Lead with the gap: opposition and experts demand rules, and the government refuses. The mechanism: commercial data brokers let a state surveil without a warrant, the same loophole fought over in the US.

stories.label: 4 vessels hit by IRGC, 3 others hit mine in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy says it struck four vessels doing ship-to-ship oil transfers in the northern Gulf at once, leaving them burning, while three more tankers hit mines overnight. Lead with the seven ships in one night; attribute the IRGC's claims (Mehr is state media, Middle East Monitor carries it independently). Mechanism: mines and strikes turn the strait into a war-risk zone, raising insurance and freight and thinning ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; tie it to Brent crude, which has rallied about $10 in two weeks. Name who pays: Asian importers and the crews aboard.

stories.label: Indian national among injured as drone debris kills two near Saudi oilfield; US orders embassy staff to leave
stories.summary: New development on the Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia: an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed two people, a Saudi citizen and an Indian resident, and injured eight, per the civil aviation authority. Lead with the dead at a civilian airport — the first deaths after the Shaybah strike and the US ordered departure we already covered. Name the victims' nationalities: South Asian migrant workers carry the risk of the Gulf war.

stories.label: Philippines Delivers Jumbo Rate Hike as Inflation Heats Up Anew
stories.summary: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas raised its benchmark rate 50 basis points to 5.50% as inflation returned and the peso weakened. Lead with the size of the hike. Mechanism: an oil importer hit by war-driven fuel prices and a sliding currency must raise borrowing costs on its own households and firms to defend the peso — the Gulf war's price arriving in Manila.

stories.label: Barclays to Cut 5,000 Jobs as AI Starts Creating Efficiency
stories.summary: Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs, about 5% of staff, in a 'technology-enabled' cost drive as it rolls out AI — announced alongside a quarter that missed estimates and a $500 million buyback. Lead with the trade: jobs cut, shareholders paid. One of the first big banks to name AI as the reason for cuts at this scale; who loses — back-office and operations staff, many in India and the UK.

stories.label: Moscow Mayor, '630 drones towards city, it's Kiev's biggest attack in 2026'
stories.summary: Moscow's mayor Sobyanin says 630 Ukrainian drones flew at the Moscow region overnight, Kyiv's biggest attack on the capital this year; 163 were downed near the city. Lead with the number, attributed to Sobyanin. The new development: it comes days after Zelensky floated freezing the front ahead of November talks with Putin — Kyiv is raising pressure, not lowering it. Report casualties and airport closures if known.

stories.label: Foragido, líder do garimpo ilegal Rodrigo Cataratas tem empresas e bens de luxo nos EUA
stories.summary: Agência Pública investigation: Rodrigo Cataratas, convicted for illegal gold mining on Yanomami land and now a fugitive for helping Alexandre Ramagem escape, holds companies and luxury assets in the United States. Lead with the assets abroad. Mechanism: wealth from mining that poisoned Yanomami rivers with mercury sits beyond Brazilian courts' reach; name the victims (the Yanomami) and ask whether Brazil has sought seizure or extradition.

stories.label: UAE's Lana Nusseibeh Enters Race for UN Secretary-General
stories.summary: The UAE formally nominated Lana Nusseibeh, its UN ambassador, for Secretary-General — a Gulf candidate entering the race while the Gulf is at war. Lead with the nomination and the field. Mechanism: the five permanent members' veto decides; weigh the Emirates' record (Sudan's RSF, Yemen) that her candidacy will face, and what an Arab woman as Secretary-General would mean for the post's rotation convention.

stories.label: 1000亿！曝DeepSeek拿下中国AI最大融资
stories.summary: DeepSeek has raised about ¥100 billion (~$15 billion), the largest funding round in Chinese AI, with CATL and Tencent among the biggest investors; it raised its target twice, from ¥50bn to ¥80bn to ¥100bn. Lead with the size. Mechanism: the open-weights lab that undercut US labs on cost now funds its own data centres and a STAR Market IPO (CITIC Securities hired) — closing the capital gap with OpenAI and Anthropic. Include its 17 October V4.1-Flash release and the open-sourced DeepInfer inference stack.

stories.label: In Brazil, Keeta Is Expanding Around the Incumbent
stories.summary: Meituan's Keeta, shut out of Rio by iFood's exclusive restaurant contracts, is opening inland Brazilian cities instead. Lead with the exclusivity wall. Mechanism: delivery platforms win on density, and exclusive deals let an incumbent lock a market — the question is whether a Chinese late entrant can build density where iFood is weak and still pay riders. Chinese platforms exporting their delivery-war playbook to the Global South, told from the mainland tech press.

stories.label: High false sign rates in transcriptome-wide association studies - Nature Genetics
stories.summary: A Nature Genetics study finds that transcriptome-wide association studies (FUSION, PrediXcan and others) — widely used to say whether a gene's higher or lower activity drives a disease — often get the direction wrong. Lead with the false sign rate. Why it matters: drug targets chosen on TWAS results could be pushed the wrong way; teach the reader how the method links genetic variants to gene expression, and where it breaks.

stories.label: Near-complete assembly of wild emmer wheat unveils centromere reorganization during polyploid evolution - Nature Genetics
stories.summary: A near-complete genome of wild emmer wheat — the Fertile Crescent ancestor of durum and bread wheat — shows centromeres were reorganised as the plant merged genomes during polyploid evolution. Lead with the finding about how the chromosomes rearranged. Why it matters: wild emmer carries drought and disease traits breeders want back in modern wheat, and a complete map shows where they sit; connect to wheat as a staple across the Middle East and North Africa.
